title: Your First Weekend at Aurora University, Shared as Cards
description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Move-In and Meet Your RA
cards.subtitle: Thursday Afternoon Arrival
cards.notes: Arrive during your assigned window to move into halls like Watkins or Memorial. Meet your Resident Assistant and get settled before the evening's hall activities begin.
cards.short_summary: The official start of the residential experience for new Spartans.
cards.evidence_claim: Freshman Move-In is scheduled for Thursday, August 27, 2026, from 1–4 p.m. for resident students.
cards.access_notes: Restricted to resident students and their families during move-in hours.

cards.title: Dinner with the Spartan Family
cards.subtitle: Thursday Evening Social
cards.notes: Join fellow new students and their families for a celebratory picnic on campus to mark the official beginning of your journey at AU.
cards.short_summary: A welcome meal for new students and families before orientation begins.
cards.evidence_claim: The Spartan Picnic is held from 5–6 p.m. on the first Thursday of Welcome Week for new students and families.
cards.access_notes: Open to all incoming students and their families.

cards.title: Official University Welcome
cards.subtitle: Friday Morning Ceremony
cards.notes: Gather with your orientation group for the official induction into the Spartan family, featuring campus spirit and introductions from university leadership.
cards.short_summary: The formal opening ceremony for the new academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: Welcome Convocation is a mandatory event for first-year students, scheduled for Friday morning at 9 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Mandatory for all incoming first-year students.

cards.title: Explore the Spartan Grounds
cards.subtitle: Friday Morning Exploration
cards.notes: Navigate the campus with your orientation group to find key landmarks and resources while completing challenges to win prizes.
cards.short_summary: An interactive way for new students to learn the campus layout.
cards.evidence_claim: A Campus Scavenger Hunt is listed as a breakout activity on Friday morning during Welcome Week.
cards.access_notes: Part of the mandatory orientation schedule for new students.

cards.title: Games and Music on the Lawn
cards.subtitle: Friday Evening Celebration
cards.notes: Celebrate your first full day on campus with food, games, music, and giveaways while meeting fellow incoming Spartans.
cards.short_summary: A social festival designed for new students to build community.
cards.evidence_claim: Freshman Fest is held from 5–8 p.m. on Friday of Welcome Week, featuring food and games.
cards.access_notes: Open to all new freshman and transfer students.

cards.title: Outdoor Cinema Night
cards.subtitle: Saturday Night Entertainment
cards.notes: Bring a blanket to the central campus lawn for a late-night movie screening under the stars with your new classmates.
cards.short_summary: A relaxed outdoor movie event held on the campus Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: Movie on the Quad is scheduled for Saturday night from 7:30–10 p.m. during Welcome Week.
cards.access_notes: Open to the campus community; late-night hours until 10 p.m.

cards.title: Find Your Classrooms
cards.subtitle: Sunday Morning Prep
cards.notes: Take your class schedule and walk through campus to locate your specific classrooms in buildings like Eckhart or Dunham Hall before Monday morning.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided tour to ensure students are ready for the first day of classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Walk Your Schedule is a designated activity on Sunday from 11 a.m.–1 p.m. to help students find their classrooms.
cards.access_notes: Self-guided; academic buildings are typically open during these hours.

cards.title: Casual Dining and Hangout
cards.subtitle: Weekend Meal Option
cards.notes: Visit the lower level of Stephens Hall for grilled sandwiches or ramen. It's a popular spot for students to eat and socialize between orientation events.
cards.short_summary: A central campus dining and social hub located in Stephens Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Spartan Spot offers grilled items and Asian-styled meals and is a primary dining option for students.
cards.access_notes: Accepts meal plans and dining points; open for lunch and dinner.

cards.title: Quiet Study and Resources
cards.subtitle: Sunday Afternoon Study
cards.notes: Explore the library's two floors, including collaborative spaces with rolling whiteboards and quiet study carrels to prepare for your first week.
cards.short_summary: The main academic library providing study spaces and technology for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Phillips Library is open on Sundays from 1 p.m.–9 p.m. during the regular semester.
cards.access_notes: Open to students with AU ID; late-night hours until 9 p.m. on Sundays.

cards.title: Reflection and Service
cards.subtitle: Weekend Quiet Space
cards.notes: Visit the Wackerlin Center for Faith and Action to find a quiet place for reflection or to learn about upcoming volunteer opportunities in the community.
cards.short_summary: A campus center dedicated to service, faith, and social justice.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wackerlin Center is a space where students gather to reflect, study, and engage in volunteer service.
cards.source_title: Wackerlin Center for Faith and Action - Aurora University
cards.access_notes: Open to all students for study and reflection.
